$comment: Per-release derived-data upgrade manifests. Schema migrations handle table SHAPE; entries here declare which DERIVED layers a release invalidates and how to recompute them. Consumed by steps_between(installed, shipped) — see topos/upgrades/__init__.py. Steps MUST be idempotent and safe to re-run after interruption.

releases.summary: Dense intelligence upgrade (stats engine, entity spine, fact store, incremental clustering, query planner). Shipped before manifests existed; entry anchors the version ladder.

Temporal entity graph (facts/goals/places/conversations materialized, provenance roles on edges, Louvain neighborhoods, semantic graph search), NER wordpiece stitcher, derived-data GC hardening, provenance split completion.

steps.title: Re-extract entities with the wordpiece stitcher
steps.why: 5f687e9 changed NER post-processing (word-level aggregation + wordpiece stitching): 1.1.0-era extractions contain ##-fragment junk and silently truncated surfaces ('Jon' for 'Jonny'). Message rows are untouched; message_entities/entity_mentions produced by the old extractor are stale.
steps.progress: TUI progress bar on the node + GET /v1/upgrade/status
steps.idempotent: record_mention is INSERT OR IGNORE; re-running converges
steps.estimated_duration: ~10–20 min per 1.5k records (CPU-bound NER); node stays usable, serves stale graph meanwhile; signal/LLM lane stays off (graph rebuild is the next step)

steps.title: Rebuild the entity graph (evidence + materialized layers)
steps.why: 1.2.0 adds layers the 1.1.0 graph never had: fact/topic/goal/place/conversation materialization, provenance role stamping on edges (attribution overlay), Louvain community ids, and GC for dangling contact anchors / orphaned facts. One rebuild derives all of it from existing data.
steps.progress: synchronous (seconds at personal scale); response is the before/after report
steps.idempotent: full-refresh semantics (mz-tagged edges rebuilt, evidence edges recomputed from mentions)
steps.$comment: Must run AFTER re-extraction completes: rebuilding from a partially restored mention set guts evidence edges (observed live 2026-07-10).

steps.title: actor_role column backfill
steps.why: Handled by the ledger-guarded schema migration actor_role_v1 at first boot; listed so release notes and the fleet dashboard show it without a manifest step.

notes: No re-embedding: the embedding model is unchanged in 1.2.0 (signal_embeddings remain valid).
No canonical re-ingest: raw and canonical rows are untouched by every 1.2.0 change.
Extraction default model moved to the quality tier (qwen3.5:9b-mlx) — affects FUTURE extractions only; small-RAM devices surface tier=stress in model recommendations and should downsize via settings.
Fleet skew: 1.1.0 nodes lack the signal_entity_graph_search handler — CPs must treat it as optional until the fleet is on 1.2.0.

releases.summary: Attention triage (daily 2x2 verdicts, badges/ranks, dashboard), negotiable time-signal availability (flex/rhythm/commitments), conversation context tags (work/personal), claim verification / fact verdicts, facts-LLM think gating.

steps.title: attention_triage_v1/v2 + conversation_context_v1 schema
steps.why: Handled by ledger-guarded / always-run schema migrations at first boot; listed so release notes and the fleet dashboard show the additive tables/columns (triage_verdicts, conversations.context_tag).

steps.title: Backfill attention triage for existing sources
steps.why: 1.3.0 adds the attention_triage enrichment job and triage_verdicts ledger. Pre-1.3.0 nodes have no verdicts or interest-profile/attention-summary objects; reprocessing fills the new derived layer from existing canonical rows without touching raw/canonical.
steps.progress: TUI progress bar on the node + GET /v1/upgrade/status
steps.idempotent: verdicts are (day, record_id) upserts; signal objects no-op when unchanged
steps.estimated_duration: seconds–minutes depending on day span; CPU-bound instruments, no LLM (signal lane off)

notes: No re-embedding and no canonical re-ingest: raw/canonical rows and signal_embeddings remain valid.

Time-signal flex/rhythm/commitment objects fill on the next scope materialization (dimension_summary / structured signal path); no dedicated rematerialize endpoint is wired into the upgrade runner yet.
Conversation context_tag columns are additive empty; owner API + local-LLM auto-label fill going forward (owner stamps always win).
Fact-extraction think suppression and claim-verify handlers affect FUTURE LLM passes only — existing signal_facts are not invalidated.

New WS handlers (signal_attention_dashboard, signal_set_worn_badge, verify_claim, conversation_context*, facts_llm_config*, truth_*, put_fact_verdict): CPs must treat as optional until the fleet is on 1.3.0; bump engine-compat when the app depends on them.

steps.why: Handled by ledger-guarded schema migrations at first boot; listed so release notes and the fleet dashboard show the additive tables/columns without a derived reprocess step.

notes: No re-embedding and no canonical re-ingest: raw/canonical rows and signal_embeddings remain valid.
Blackhole filtering is runtime policy over existing data — no backfill step.
Complexity snapshots fill via enrichment piggyback going forward; pre-1.3.2 nodes get coverage on the next enrichment pass.

releases.summary: Release migration hardening (PLAN_NODE_RELEASE_MIGRATIONS M0–M2) + attention pin/retire intent handlers.

steps.title: Single migration registry + backup + downgrade guard
steps.why: PLAN_NODE_RELEASE_MIGRATIONS M0–M2: unify apply/ensure on one MIGRATIONS registry, PRAGMA user_version fast-path, fail-loud on shape failures, pre-migration backup under ~/.topos/backups, downgrade guard when user_version is ahead of this build. No derived-layer invalidation.

notes: Code + schema-runner only — raw/canonical/derived rows are untouched.
Nodes upgrading into this release get a pre-migration backup when ledger-pending migrations exist.
Also ships signal_pin_intent / signal_retire_intent (protocol + code only; no derived invalidation).

releases.summary: PLAN M3–M4: coverage spec_version stamps, selective anti-join, new upgrade executors + consent, upgrade-matrix CI.

steps.title: Coverage spec_version + selective anti-join
steps.why: PLAN M3: additive spec_version on coverage tables; catalog JOB_SPEC_VERSIONS; writers stamp; anti-join treats NULL as 0. Current catalog versions all start at 1 — no derived wipe required.

notes: Also ships canonical_reprocess / derived_rebuild / reembed executors and pending_consent for slow steps.
M4: scripts/build_upgrade_fixture.py + run_upgrade_matrix.py + upgrade-matrix.yml.

releases.summary: Pin torch<2.13; no schema or data change.
notes: Dependency-only. No migration, no reprocessing, no consent prompt: nothing on disk changes shape, so `steps` is deliberately empty.

torch 2.13.0 segfaulted the node under concurrent MPS use (embedder + privacy filter + NSFW classifier), which is what a first chat query triggers. Upgrading is safe from any prior version and needs no user action beyond the restart the upgrade already performs.

releases.summary: Inbox txn hygiene + coalesce deferred enrichment; topic clustering off-loop; sanitization prewarm progress on upgrade/shell status; macOS computer_name in system_info. Code-only / protocol-additive.

Stability release: write-gate/event-loop deadlock class eliminated (control-plane client on its own thread), entity-graph rebuild in a subprocess (no more ~100s healthcheck darkness), repo-wide gated SQLite writes (73 files), startup DB work on a dedicated worker thread with the owner-connection swap serialized. Signal-registry upgrade jobs now route down the signal lane; one manifest step redoes the 1.3.0 attention-triage backfill that no-opped. Code-only otherwise.

steps.title: Re-run the attention triage backfill (1.3.0 step was a routing no-op)
steps.why: The 1.3.0 backfill-attention-triage step ledgered 'done' on every node without writing a single verdict: attention_triage lives in SIGNAL_DERIVATION_JOBS, but the runner routed it through run_canonical(), which filters job_names against CANONICAL_JOBS and silently dropped it. Nodes that upgraded through 1.3.0–1.3.6 therefore have a green ledger row and zero backfilled triage history. The runner now routes signal-registry jobs down the narrow signal lane; this step re-declares the backfill so already-upgraded nodes are healed too. Days triaged organically since 1.3.0 no-op via the (day, record_id) upserts.
steps.progress: TUI progress bar on the node + GET /v1/upgrade/status
steps.idempotent: verdicts are (day, record_id) upserts; signal objects no-op when unchanged
steps.estimated_duration: measured ~0.7s per day of history on a real node (no LLM, no network); minutes at worst for multi-year nodes

releases.summary: Stability: ingest/enrichment DB writes off the event loop; statistics job no longer holds an open write lock across the pipeline; graph refresher skips cross-thread dirty bumps; open-txn watchdog (opt-in); DMG in-app update finds bundled uv; control-plane pong deadline restored. Code-only.
notes: Code-only — no schema migration, no derived-layer invalidation, no consent prompt.
Worker-thread write offload + statistics txn hygiene close the database-is-locked / event-loop-stall class that hit repeat ingests after 1.3.7.

releases.summary: Derivation-retry repair: the signal_derive_retry executor was never registered, so every recorded derivation debt was claimed and failed as an unknown job kind — the retry meant to repair a lost derivation destroyed the record of it instead. The executor is wired, workers claim only kinds they can execute, and an executor may requeue rather than read as failed. One consent:auto step sweeps debt already parked 'failed', which nothing else would re-queue. Also: public_bio:read / work_context:read gain test cover for the restored profile_records lane, and just harness-gate scores answer quality against a ratcheting floor instead of a 70/70 bar it cannot reach on a signal-less seed DB. No schema change.

steps.title: Re-run derivation debt that was failed as an unknown job kind
steps.why: record_failed_derivation() has enqueued pipeline rows of kind 'signal_derive_retry' since 1.3.x, but no executor was ever registered for that kind, so the worker claimed each row and immediately failed it with 'Unknown job kind: signal_derive_retry'. The debt record IS the queue row, so the retry meant to repair a lost derivation destroyed the record of it instead — nodes carry silent derivation gaps with a 'failed' row and nothing pointing at them. The executor is registered as of this release, but that does not revive the existing rows: a failed row is only re-queued by the next organic failure of the same (batch, job), and recover_stale_jobs resets 'running' rows, never 'failed' ones. This step sweeps them once on upgrade so the repair happens without an operator remembering to POST /v1/signal/derivation-debt/retry.
steps.cost: no LLM, no network; re-runs only the derivations already recorded as lost
steps.progress: synchronous; response is the attempted/recovered/still_failing report
steps.idempotent: re-running is a no-op once pending is empty; a debt that fails again is left 'failed' and still listed
steps.estimated_duration: seconds on a node with no debt (the common case); proportional to recorded debt otherwise

releases.summary: Ingest throughput: the conversation auto-classifier stops re-asking the same unlabelable conversations on every enrichment batch (~20 model calls / ~26s per batch, permanently, for zero progress). An unclear verdict now retires the row instead of being silently dropped. No steps: nothing on-node is invalidated — prompt, model and parse logic are unchanged, so existing auto: tags remain valid, and retired rows self-heal on the next enrichment pass.

Graph time correctness: edges stop being dated by when the machine touched them. Co-occurrence rebuilds no longer restart each edge's belief clock (valid_from); topic-cluster edges take the attribution role of their member records instead of defaulting to 'authored'; journal entry_at written from the import clock is re-dated from starts_at; and DATE/TIME/CARDINAL surfaces are no longer minted as graph nodes. Also: a failed upgrade step is reachable for retry again (ledger rows key on the DECLARING release, and the plan carries any step short of 'done'), and a progress bar can no longer fail the step it narrates.

steps.title: Re-date journal entries that recorded the import clock as their event time
steps.why: Grow's journal producers wrote entry_at from the import clock while the true session time sat in starts_at. On the first live node checked: 309 rows across two sources, 127 of them sharing 2026-08-08T03:34:44 to the second, with real sessions spanning months. The entity graph dates its edges from canonical event time, so those batches pulled years-old relationships into the recent graph window. SQLiteCanonicalStore._journal_entry_at closes this for new writes, but a row already on disk only moves if something sweeps it. The predicate IS the corruption signature (entry_at equal to ingested_at to the second, with a real starts_at present), so a genuine entry_at is never touched and the step is safe to re-run. The timeline projection is unaffected either way: it already reads starts_at, so this brings entry_at into agreement with what timeline always showed.
steps.cost: no LLM, no network; one bounded UPDATE over journal_entries
steps.idempotent: the signature stops matching once a row is repaired

steps.title: Rebuild the entity graph so edges pick up the corrected dates, roles and value-surface guard
steps.why: Three of this release's fixes only reach EXISTING data through a rebuild: co-occurrence edges stop having their belief clock (valid_from) restarted on every rebuild; topic-cluster edges stop defaulting to actor_role 'authored' and take the role of their member records instead; and DATE/TIME/CARDINAL surfaces ('an hour', 'this week', 'four') are no longer minted as graph nodes, with previously-minted ones purged. It must run AFTER the journal date repair, because rebuilding first would only re-derive edges from the uncorrected event times.
steps.cost: no LLM, no network; the rebuild runs in a subprocess so the node's event loop stays live
steps.progress: TUI progress bar on the node + GET /v1/upgrade/status
steps.estimated_duration: measured ~124s on a real node (2,741 edges)

notes: Graph time-window RCA (2026-08-10): five defects, all variations on recording when the machine touched the data rather than when the thing happened.
The scrub-window fix ships in topos-react-app, not here.

releases.summary: Owner curation and search stop reporting how many times something was stored. The People tab's duplicate queue asked one question per sighting rather than per decision (8,134 pending rows for 99 real decisions on a live node), derivation asked about strings the owner never said, candidates never seen in the data were offered as merge targets (contacts included), and possessives, trailing punctuation and redaction placeholders were treated as identities. Search returned the same text once per time it was stored, where 37% of a live corpus is duplicate text. Orphan cleanup also stopped reaping the graph vertices derivation had just minted, which had been churning 173 entities and 206 edges per scrub. No steps: the three entity_review migrations run at boot and collapse the queue in place, preserving every prior answer and unbind guard; the spine and search changes are code-only and take effect on the next resolve and the next query.
notes: Migrations 57-59 delete duplicate and unanswerable entity_review rows and mark the rest stale; approved, dismissed and no_bind rows are never touched.

Entity labels already minted with a possessive, trailing dash or [NAME] are left in place — they surface through the review queue as ordinary merge decisions rather than being rewritten underneath the owner.
The occurrences count on search results ships in topos-react-app as well.

releases.summary: Staging entry for in-flight PRs. cut_release.py stamps this with the next version at release cut. Never executed by steps_between.

steps.title: Backfill embeddings for browser activity rows the stale-install gate dropped
steps.why: A 2026-05-29 source_runtime_installs snapshot for browser_visits/browser_events (enrichment_trigger='manual', no jobs) shadowed the bundled lane policy from the ~2026-07-10 deploy on: every live browser push since ran zero enrichment/signal jobs while the inbox job reported done (one live node: 0/1,034 August visits embedded). Runtime installs now adopt bundled lane policy, but rows ingested while the gate was closed still have no derived data.
steps.idempotent: coverage-driven row selection (only rows missing derived output); embedding writes are (record_id, model, chunk_index)-keyed with content-hash skip, and activity rows dedupe to one vector per distinct text, so re-running converges
steps.cost: local models only, no network; ~1k title-length rows on the affected node, minutes on the local embedding model; unaffected sources no-op on the coverage check

steps.title: Re-map retained GitHub push events so activity rows carry their commit messages
steps.why: activity_events.content was NULL on every github push row (one live node: 451/451, and only 11 DISTINCT titles across all 451 — all '{owner}/{repo}: pushed N commit'), because the mapper carried repo/actor and nothing else, and the store's INSERT did not list the content column at all. The commit messages — the only text that says what the work WAS — sat unused in the retained raw payloads. Everything semantic downstream could therefore match on repo NAME alone: goal/interest attachment to engineering work was pure name matching, and a contrastive term extraction over commit-attached items returned nothing but 'pushed'/'commit'. The declared field map and the store fix land in this release, but neither reaches a row already on disk: re-mapping from raw retention is what fills it. Raw retention holds the full PushEvent payloads (461 rows on the same node), so no re-fetch from GitHub is needed.
steps.idempotent: re-mapping is upsert-keyed (activity event_id, journal entry_id) and content is written with COALESCE, so re-running rewrites the same values
steps.cost: no network, no models: one parse + upsert per retained raw row (458 on the measured node), seconds. Nodes with no github_activity install no-op
steps.$comment: CANONICAL ONLY (run_enrichment: false), deliberately. The default fan-out would run this source's baseline signal jobs, and a 458-row batch exceeds topic_clusters' _INCREMENTAL_MAX_BATCH (200), which forces a FULL cluster recompute: on the measured node that repartitions all 152 clusters, and 85 of them (interests 48, wellbeing 27, memory 10) sit in dimensions whose definitions/<dimension>.json is not yet in the tree, so dimension_core_question falls back to the generic prompt silently. Corrected content is what this release owes; derivation over it belongs to the release that lands the topic-dimension work, as one pass with the definitions present rather than two with a repartition in between.

steps.title: Rename existing topic clusters with the contrastive, dimension-framed labeler
steps.why: Cluster labels were generated one cluster at a time from that cluster's own most frequent terms, under one generic instruction regardless of which signal dimension the cluster was built in. On one live node that left 152 clusters carrying 91 distinct labels — 'personal projects' on fourteen of them spanning five dimensions, 'private notes' on five — which is what every surface that lists topics showed. The new prompt reaches an existing cluster only through a relabel: nothing about its membership changed, so no other stage will rewrite these names on its own. Labels ONLY, deliberately — a full recompute would relabel but also repartition (seed-to-seed ARI ~0.52 on the live corpus), churning cluster ids, top_topics facts and UI links for what is a prompt change.
steps.idempotent: labels and label metadata only — cluster ids, membership and centroids are untouched, and the deterministic term label is preserved in metadata.term_label. Re-running renames from the same inputs; the local model is sampled, so a second run can word the same clusters differently.
steps.cost: one short local-LLM call per cluster, plus one retry per duplicate name; measured ~2s per call on llama3.2:latest (~6 min for 152 clusters). No network. Nodes with no clusters no-op.

steps.title: Re-run every black-hole rebuild so it reaches topic cluster labels and member excerpts
steps.why: The black-hole rebuild withdraws prose artifacts naming a protected entity, but topic_clusters and topic_cluster_members were never on its list — the label used to be term soup that named nobody, and the contrastive labeler now names the subject (33 of 152 labels on one live node were an entity name). The rebuild also had to learn that the cluster ROW is the producer: closing the derived top_topics object alone is undone by the next cluster pass, which re-mints the fact from topic_clusters.label. Existing black holes are marked 'complete', so run_pending_rebuilds skips exactly the entities carrying the un-withdrawn data: the same live node had five member excerpts still quoting a protected entity under three completed rebuilds. Must run AFTER relabel-topic-clusters so it also sees anything that pass just wrote.
steps.idempotent: withdrawal is a name scan re-applied to whatever is currently stored; a second run finds nothing left to withdraw. Cluster ids, membership and counts are untouched — only prose (label, centroid preview, member excerpts) is withdrawn.
steps.cost: no LLM, no network; a scan of topic_clusters, topic_cluster_members, signal_objects and briefs per protected entity. Seconds. Nodes with no black holes no-op.

steps.title: Re-run dimension_summary where undeclared PlaceContext writes failed the whole job
steps.why: The artifact router writes PlaceContext objects into the places dimension for every place EntityRef, but places.json never declared the type, so SignalObjectStore rejected the write and dimension_summary DEGRADED on any batch containing a place reference — the derivation-retry ledger recorded the debt but nothing consumes it automatically. Observed on grow_data_file 2026-08-15: every manual-enrichment batch (171 records) queued for retry with derived data MISSING. places.json now declares PlaceContext, so a re-run succeeds where the same records failed.
steps.idempotent: coverage-driven row selection (only records whose dimension_summary output is missing); signal object upserts are (dimension, object_type, object_key)-keyed and supersede in place, so re-running converges
steps.cost: local models only, no network; scoped to records whose derived output is missing — the failed grow_data_file batches on the affected node, minutes; unaffected sources no-op on the coverage check

steps.title: url_classification retired; its table and interest tags removed
steps.why: The job classified visited pages into DMOZ top-level categories. On the node this was measured on it produced 8,616 rows over six months, 73% of them the single label 'Reference' at an average confidence of 0.961 — HIGHER than any other bucket, so no threshold separates it from filler. The same host drew different labels on different visits (github.com: Reference 720, Computers 125, Kids 5), because the classifier reads the page title and an authenticated app title says almost nothing. DMOZ describes where a site files in a directory, not what a person is doing; 'Reference' is its catch-all. 458 of the interests dimension's 828 signal objects were these tags, 349 of them 'Reference'. Handled by the ledger-guarded migration retire_url_classification_v1 at first boot; listed so release notes and the fleet dashboard show it without a step. Scoped by payload source_kind, so the materializer's keyword-rule tags and the personal fact objects that also live in interests are untouched — verified on a copy of a live node: 828 -> 370 interests objects, facts 6 -> 6, other dimensions 6,580 unchanged.

notes: Deploying this build requires reinstalling the node (frozen uv tool snapshot) — a plain restart runs the old code and leaves the browser lanes dark.
Existing clusters keep their old labels until relabel-topic-clusters runs: the labeler runs at cluster write time, and this release changes the prompt, not the partition.

Nodes whose github raw retention was purged keep NULL content on their old push rows; new pushes carry commit messages from this build on. Browser rows written before this release keep NULL content/hostname until they are re-ingested — no raw-retention re-map step is declared for them because the plugin re-pushes visits organically.
